advice: Indian law enforcement agencies (Police, CBI, ED, Customs) never conduct arrests or interrogations over Skype, WhatsApp, or video calls.
Immediately disconnect the video call. Do not transfer any funds or show your bank accounts.
Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 or file an immediate complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
Banks and telecom operators never send links asking to update KYC, PAN, or SIM details via SMS.
Do not click the link or download any APK file (e.g. AnyDesk, QuickSupport, SBI_KYC.apk).
If you already entered banking details, immediately contact your bank customer care to freeze your netbanking and card.
Remember: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN or scan a QR code to RECEIVE money.
Scanning a QR code or entering your UPI PIN always deducts money from your account.
Report the scammer's UPI ID and phone number in your UPI app (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, BHIM).
No legitimate stock, crypto, or institutional investment scheme guarantees 200% to 500% returns.
Exit the Telegram or WhatsApp investment group immediately. Do not transfer funds to personal or unverified UPI accounts.
Report the group admins and fraudulent trading websites to cybercrime.gov.in.
Customs and courier companies (FedEx, DHL, India Post) never demand fines or clearance fees into personal UPI or bank accounts.
Do not believe claims that a parcel with illegal contraband or passports was shipped under your name.
Verify directly with the official courier customer care using their official website.
Legitimate employers never ask you to pay a deposit, registration fee, or buy cryptocurrency to receive daily task wages.
Do not send money or complete 'paid tasks' (YouTube likes, hotel reviews, Google maps rating).
Block the sender and report the group on Telegram/WhatsApp.
You cannot win a lottery or lucky draw you never bought a ticket for (e.g. KBC, Kaun Banega Crorepati).
Never pay 'processing fees', 'GST', or 'clearance charges' to claim a prize.
Block the sender number and delete the message.
Illegal instant loan apps access your contact list and blackmail your family and colleagues.
Do not pay extorted amounts. File an immediate complaint on cybercrime.gov.in with screenshots of threats.
File a police complaint at your local cyber cell and inform your close contacts about the blackmail scheme.
State electricity boards (BESCOM, TNEB, MSEDCL, UPPCL) never send disconnection threats from personal 10-digit mobile numbers.
Do not call the phone number mentioned in the SMS or pay via third-party payment links.
Check your bill status only on the official electricity utility portal or mobile app.
Scammers post fake customer care numbers on Google search, Google Maps, and social media.
Customer support executives never ask you to install remote control apps like AnyDesk or TeamViewer.
Always obtain customer care telephone numbers directly from the official back of your credit/debit card or verified official website.
Bank employees never call you asking for OTPs, CVV, Netbanking passwords, or Card PINs.
Never share OTP with anyone, even if the caller claims your card is blocked or points are expiring.
If you accidentally shared an OTP, call your bank immediately to block all transactions.
Do not panic and DO NOT pay any extortion money. Paying once leads to endless demands.
Block the blackmailer immediately across all platforms (WhatsApp, Skype, Instagram).
File an immediate report on cybercrime.gov.in and report intimate imagery to StopNCII.org.
Be cautious of unsolicited messages urging immediate action or offering unexpected financial rewards.
Never share passwords, OTPs, or click suspicious links received from unknown senders.
For cyber fraud emergencies, dial 1930 immediately or visit cybercrime.gov.in.
